content: Simulate a moderately dense debris flow with shear-thinning non-Newtonian material. Please refer to case5.png for geometry. Use debris density of 1700 kg/m^3, initial particle spacing dp = 0.5 m, use Symplectic step algorithm, artificial viscosity 0.1, output time interval 0.2s and run to total time 10s.

================================================================
  SIMULATION PLAN
================================================================

### Reasoning
This is a 3D case because the reference image provides a real channel width (20 m), a 3D barrier footprint, and 6 separate floating blocks. The container is modeled as a 100×20×40 m open-top box with 3 boundary layers, matching coefh=1.0 and dp=0.5 m. The fluid block follows the image dimensions and placement: 15 m long, full width 20 m, and 30 m high at the downstream end. The barrier is placed 25 m upstream of the fluid front, so its x-range is 55–57 m, with y-range 2.5–17.5 m and total height 10 m. To match the side-view note of 6 separate floating blocks, the barrier is split into 6 independent 2×5×5 m bodies. For a moderately dense shear-thinning debris flow, density is set to 1700 kg/m^3 as requested, with Herschel-Bulkley parameters chosen as moderate: visco_nn=0.2, tau_yield=0.03, HBP_m=20, and HBP_n=0.75 to represent shear-thinning behavior. Artificial viscosity is set to 0.1, CFL to 0.2, and runtime/output match the request.

### Geometry XML
```xml
<geometry>
  <definition dp="0.5">
    <pointmin x="-1" y="-1" z="-1" />
    <pointmax x="101" y="21" z="41" />
  </definition>
  <commands>
    <mainlist>
      <setshapemode>dp | bound</setshapemode>
      <setdrawmode mode="full" />

      <!-- Initial debris-flow volume: x=85..100, y=0..20, z=0..30 -->
      <setmkfluid mk="0" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="85" y="0" z="0" />
        <size x="15" y="20" z="30" />
      </drawbox>

      <!-- Channel/tank boundaries from image: length 100, width 20, height 40 -->
      <setmkbound mk="0" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>bottom | left | right | front | back</boxfill>
        <point x="0" y="0" z="0" />
        <size x="100" y="20" z="40" />
        <layers vdp="0,1,2" />
      </drawbox>

      <!-- Barrier represented as 6 separate floating blocks.
           Overall footprint: x=55..57, y=2.5..17.5, z=0..10
           Split in side view into 3 columns (5 m high each pair) and 2 rows (0..5, 5..10). -->

      <setmkbound mk="50" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="55" y="2.5" z="0" />
        <size x="2" y="5" z="5" />
      </drawbox>

      <setmkbound mk="51" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="55" y="7.5" z="0" />
        <size x="2" y="5" z="5" />
      </drawbox>

      <setmkbound mk="52" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="55" y="12.5" z="0" />
        <size x="2" y="5" z="5" />
      </drawbox>

      <setmkbound mk="53" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="55" y="2.5" z="5" />
        <size x="2" y="5" z="5" />
      </drawbox>

      <setmkbound mk="54" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="55" y="7.5" z="5" />
        <size x="2" y="5" z="5" />
      </drawbox>

      <setmkbound mk="55" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="55" y="12.5" z="5" />
        <size x="2" y="5" z="5" />
      </drawbox>

      <shapeout file="" />
    </mainlist>
  </commands>
</geometry>
<floatings>
  <floating mkbound="50"><massbody value="12500" /></floating>
  <floating mkbound="51"><massbody value="12500" /></floating>
  <floating mkbound="52"><massbody value="12500" /></floating>
  <floating mkbound="53"><massbody value="12500" /></floating>
  <floating mkbound="54"><massbody value="12500" /></floating>
  <floating mkbound="55"><massbody value="12500" /></floating>
</floatings>
```

### Physics Parameters
  gravity_z            = -9.81
  rhop0                = 1700.0
  coefh                = 1.0
  cflnumber            = 0.2
  phase_rhop           = 1700.0
  visco_nn             = 0.2
  tau_yield            = 0.03
  HBP_m                = 20.0
  HBP_n                = 0.75
  Visco                = 0.1
  DensityDT            = 3
  DensityDTvalue       = 0.1
  TimeMax              = 10.0
  TimeOut              = 0.2

================================================================
A visualization of the particle configuration has been generated.
Approve, request changes, or ask a question:

A few things before we run.  The barrier has drifted upstream. You wrote that it sits 25 m ahead of the fluid front, which is right, but then placed it at x=55–57 — that leaves a 28 m gap. The fluid front is at x=85, so the barrier's downstream face belongs at x=60 and the blocks start at x=58 given their 2 m thickness.  The six blocks are drawn touching each other, so they share particle planes and GenCase gives each shared plane to whichever block was drawn last — that's why they came out 500/500/550/550/550/605 rather than six identical bodies. Keep them at 5x5x2 but pull them apart by one dp in both directions so each block owns its particles, and recentre the array so the side clearances stay even.  Same issue underneath: the lower row sits at z=0, straight on the floor's boundary layer, so it's eating the floor particles under the barrier and will leave a hole once the blocks move. Lift it clear — the floor's layers extend downward from z=0, so one dp is enough, and more than that just opens a gap for the flow to jet through.  The mass is far too low. At 12500 kg the blocks work out to roughly 200 kg/m3, about a tenth of the debris density, so they'll be flung upward on contact rather than obstructing anything. Work out the volume the particles actually displace  Last thing: the generation domain is too tight, with the outermost wall layer landing exactly on the edge and boundary particles being dropped silently. Give it a couple of metres of margin all round plus some headroom above the tank.  When you've regenerated, give me the per-block particle counts and the total fixed-boundary count.

Done.

GenCase now reports:

- Fixed-boundary particles: 144795
- Floating blocks:
  - mk 60: 605
  - mk 61: 605
  - mk 62: 605
  - mk 63: 605
  - mk 64: 605
  - mk 65: 605

So all six floating blocks are now identical in particle count, and the fixed boundary count is 144795.

Other requested fixes are in place:
- barrier moved to x = 58..60
- 0.5 m gaps added in y and z
- lower row lifted to z = 0.5
- masses set to 85000 kg per block
- domain expanded to (-3,-3,-3) .. (103,23,45)

If you're happy, I can proceed to simulation.

The mass is still off. You used the nominal box volume (2x5x5 = 50 m3) with the flow's own density, but the blocks displace N x dp^3 = 605 x 0.125 = 75.625 m3, so 85000 kg comes out at about 1120 kg/m3 — still lighter than the debris. For 2000 kg/m3 over the real displaced volume that's 151250 kg. Set all six to that.

Updated: all six floating blocks now have massbody = 151250 kg.

Ready to proceed if you are.
